name: Sensorineural Deafness with Dilated Cardiomyopathy
aliases: Sensorineural Hearing Loss and Dilated Cardiomyopathy Syndrome

criteria.description: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss confirmed by audiometry
Echocardiographic evidence of dilated cardiomyopathy with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction
Exclusion of other known causes of sensorineural deafness and cardiomyopathy
Positive family history of sensorineural deafness and/or cardiomyopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and echocardiographic evidence of dilated cardiomyopathy with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but no specific gene identified universally

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP indicating heart failure
imaging: Echocardiogram showing dilated left ventricle with reduced ejection fraction
Cardiac MRI may show myocardial fibrosis
genetic: Possible mutations in mitochondrial or nuclear genes affecting both cardiac and auditory function (gene testing recommended but no definitive gene identified)
other: Audiometry confirming bilateral sensorineural hearing loss
Electrocardiogram showing arrhythmias or conduction abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic testing identifying specific causative mutations
Additional systemic features depending on subtype

redFlags: Rapid progression of heart failure symptoms
Sudden onset of syncope or cardiac arrest
Severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss in early childhood
references: Orphanet: Sensorineural deafness with dilated cardiomyopathy (ORPHA:217622)
Maron BJ, Towbin JA, Thiene G, et al. Contemporary definitions and classification of the cardiomyopathies. Circulation. 2006;113(14):1807-1816.
Shearer AE, Hildebrand MS, Smith RJH. Hereditary Hearing Loss and Deafness Overview. GeneReviews® [Internet]. 1999.
